title: The Floor Under Every Overnight Rate
subtitle: Watch the ON RRP facility drain reserves and set the price of cash.

challenges.prompt: Why does the ON RRP facility put a floor under overnight rates?
challenges.explanation: A money market fund cannot hold reserves, so without ON RRP it must lend to banks at whatever they offer. The facility gives it a risk-free alternative at a published rate — so it will not lend below that rate to anyone.

options.label: It gives non-banks a risk-free rate they can always take instead
It caps how much banks are allowed to charge each other
options.feedback: Nothing here is a price control. The floor works by competition, not by rule.

options.label: It creates new reserves for money market funds
options.feedback: The opposite: cash parked at the ON RRP window drains reserves out of the banking system.

challenges.prompt: A money market fund parks $500M at the Fed's ON RRP window overnight.
challenges.instructions: Post the entries on all three sheets. Nothing grows here — watch what moves instead.
challenges.scenario: The fund pulls $500M out of its bank deposit and lends it to the Fed overnight against Treasury collateral.
challenges.explanation: Total Fed liabilities are unchanged: $500M simply moved from the reserves line to the reverse repo line. But reserves are base money and reverse repos are not, so the banking system is $500M smaller while the Fed's sheet is the same size.

options.feedback: The Fed pledges the collateral, it does not sell it. Its Treasury holdings are untouched overnight.
Reserves fall here. The cash left the banking system for the Fed's own window.
Money market funds are not banks — they cannot hold reserves. That is the whole reason ON RRP exists.

aggregateEffects.note: Reserves fell by $500M. Reverse repos are a Fed liability too, but they are not base money.
A bank deposit disappeared. Whether headline M2 moves depends on whether this fund's own shares are counted in it.

keyTakeaways: The ON RRP window drains reserves without shrinking the Fed's balance sheet.
A facility open to non-banks sets the floor the whole overnight market prices against.
Composition of central bank liabilities matters as much as their total.
